    The Euler characteristic of the three-term complex of morphisms #

    source
    theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.TwoTerm.bounded_hom_euler (k : Type u) [Field k] {R : Type u} [Ring R] [Algebra k R] [IsNoetherianRing R] (P Q : TwoTerm R) [Module.Finite k R] :
    have h := fun (n : ℤ) => ↑(Module.finrank k (P.inBoundedProjectives ⟶ (CategoryTheory.shiftFunctor (boundedProjective R).FullSubcategory n).obj Q.inBoundedProjectives)); h 0 - h (-1) - h 1 = ↑(Module.finrank k (P.source ⟶ Q.source)) + ↑(Module.finrank k (P.target ⟶ Q.target)) - ↑(Module.finrank k (P.target ⟶ Q.source)) - ↑(Module.finrank k (P.source ⟶ Q.target))

    Euler characteristic of the Hom complex on two projective differentials.

    source
    theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.TwoTerm.pencil_hom_finrank_le (k : Type u) [Field k] {R : Type u} [Ring R] [Algebra k R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [Module.Finite k R] {A B : FGModuleCat R} [Module.Projective R ↑A] [Module.Projective R ↑B] (u σ : A ⟶ B) (hu : (ofDifferential u).IsPresilting) (V : TwoTerm R) (n : ℤ) :
    have U := (ofDifferential u).inBoundedProjectives; have S := (ofDifferential σ).inBoundedProjectives; have W := V.inBoundedProjectives; Module.finrank k (U ⟶ (CategoryTheory.shiftFunctor (boundedProjective R).FullSubcategory n).obj W) ≤ Module.finrank k (S ⟶ (CategoryTheory.shiftFunctor (boundedProjective R).FullSubcategory n).obj W) ∧ Module.finrank k (W ⟶ (CategoryTheory.shiftFunctor (boundedProjective R).FullSubcategory n).obj U) ≤ Module.finrank k (W ⟶ (CategoryTheory.shiftFunctor (boundedProjective R).FullSubcategory n).obj S)

    On the fixed terms of a two-term presilting complex, any change of differential weakly increases both Hom dimensions in every integer shift.
